// unizik-ml-fraud-frontend/src/app/api/checkout/route.ts

  

import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';

import { headers } from 'next/headers';

import { z } from 'zod';

import { prisma } from '@/lib/prisma';

import { evaluatePaymentTransaction } from '@/lib/fraud-engine';

  

// Payload schema: Client reports what it can measure (timing,
fingerprinting).

// Server detects what it can prove (IP, ASN/Telco, Location).

const checkoutSchema = z.object({

  studentId: z.string().uuid(),

  invoiceId: z.string().uuid(),

  amount: z.number().positive(),

  reference: z.string().min(6),

  deviceId: z.string().min(8),

  pageDwellTime: z.number().positive(),

  hardwareMismatch: z.number().int().min(0).max(1),

});

  

/\*\*

 \* PRODUCTION NETWORK DETECTOR

 \* Detects if the user is on a Nigerian Telco (MTN, Glo, Airtel,
9Mobile).

 \* If not, flags as high risk (asnNumber = 1).

 \*/

async function getNetworkRiskScore(ip: string): Promise\<number\> {

  // 1. Localhost Handling

  if (ip === "127.0.0.1" \|\| ip === "::1" \|\|
ip.startsWith("192.168.")) return 0; // Safe in dev

  

  try {

    // Using free, no-key API: ip-api.com

    const response = await
fetch(\`http://ip-api.com/json/\${ip}?fields=status,isp,query\`);

    const data = await response.json();

  

    if (data.status !== "success") return 1; // Flag as risk if we can't
resolve IP

  

    const ispName = data.isp.toUpperCase();

    const telcos = \["MTN", "GLOBACOM", "AIRTEL", "9MOBILE",
"ETISALAT"\];

  

    // Check if the ISP string includes any of our whitelisted Nigerian
Telcos

    const isLocalTelco = telcos.some(telco =\> ispName.includes(telco));

  

    return isLocalTelco ? 0 : 1; // 0 = Safe (Local), 1 = Risky
(VPN/Foreign/Other)

  } catch (e) {

    console.error("\[NETWORK DETECTION ERROR\]", e);

    return 1; // Default to risky if detection fails

  }

}

  

export async function POST(req: Request) {

  try {

    const headersList = await headers();

    // Get real IP from headers

    const rawIp = headersList.get('x-forwarded-for') \|\| '127.0.0.1';

    const ipAddress = rawIp.split(',')\[0\]; // Handle proxy chains

  

    const body = await req.json();

    const validation = checkoutSchema.safeParse(body);

  

    if (!validation.success) {

      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Validation
Failed", details: validation.error }, { status: 400 });

    }

  

    // Server-side network risk assessment

    const asnNumber = await getNetworkRiskScore(ipAddress);

  

    // Merge client telemetry with server-derived network metadata

    const payload = {

      ...validation.data,

      ipAddress,

      asnNumber, // ENFORCED: Server overrides client's asnNumber

    };

  

    // 1. FINANCIAL INTEGRITY GUARDRAIL

    const invoice = await prisma.feeInvoice.findUnique({ where: { id:
payload.invoiceId } });

    if (!invoice \|\| invoice.studentId !== payload.studentId \|\|
invoice.amount !== payload.amount) {

      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Invalid or
Tampered Invoice" }, { status: 403 });

    }

    if (invoice.status === 'PAID') {

      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "This fee
invoice has already been cleared and marked as PAID in the university
records." }, { status: 400 });

    }

  

    // 2. DISPATCH TO ML ENGINE

    const engineResult = await evaluatePaymentTransaction(payload);

  

    // Use upsert to prevent "Unique constraint failed" on reference
collisions

    // and fix the status enum to match your schema ('CLEARED' vs
'SUCCESS')

    const tx = await prisma.transaction.upsert({

      where: { reference: payload.reference },

      update: {},

      create: {

        invoiceId: payload.invoiceId,

        studentId: payload.studentId,

        amount: payload.amount,

        reference: payload.reference,

        deviceId: payload.deviceId,

        ipAddress: payload.ipAddress,

        asnNumber: payload.asnNumber,

        pageDwellTime: payload.pageDwellTime,

        hardwareMismatch: payload.hardwareMismatch,

        status: engineResult.verdict === 'FRAUDULENT' ? 'BLOCKED' :
'CLEARED'

      }

    });

  

    if (engineResult.verdict === 'FRAUDULENT') {

      // CRITICAL PATH B ENFORCEMENT: Freeze the parent invoice
immediately

      await prisma.feeInvoice.update({

        where: { id: payload.invoiceId },

        data: { status: 'BLOCKED' as any }

      });

  

      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, message: "Blocked",
forensicReport: engineResult }, { status: 403 });

    }

  

    return NextResponse.json({ success: true, message: "Authorized",
data: { id: tx.id } }, { status: 200 });

  } catch (error: any) {

    console.error("\[CHECKOUT ROUTE ERROR\]:", error.message);

    return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Internal Error"
}, { status: 500 });

  }

}

  

  

// unizik-ml-fraud-frontend/src/app/api/invoices/route.ts

  

import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';

import { prisma } from '@/lib/prisma';

import { FeeCategory, InvoiceStatus } from '@prisma/client';

  

// Official UNIZIK Fee Schedule (Server-Enforced to prevent client-side
price tampering)

const OFFICIAL_FEE_SCHEDULE: Record\<FeeCategory, number\> = {

  TUITION: 85500.00,

  ACCEPTANCE: 45000.00,

  ICT_INFRASTRUCTURE: 15000.00,

  LIBRARY: 5000.00,

  EXAM_CLEARANCE: 10000.00,

};

  

// GET: Fetch all invoices for a specific student UUID

export async function GET(req: Request) {

  try {

    const { searchParams } = new URL(req.url);

    const studentId = searchParams.get('studentId');

    const invoiceId = searchParams.get('invoiceId');

   

    if (invoiceId) {

        const invoice = await prisma.feeInvoice.findUnique({ where: {
id: invoiceId } });

        return NextResponse.json({ success: true, invoice });

    }

    if (!studentId) {

      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Student UUID is
required." }, { status: 400 });

    }

  

    const invoices = await prisma.feeInvoice.findMany({

      where: { studentId },

      orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' },

      include: {

        transactions: {

          orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' },

          take: 1, // Include the most recent transaction attempt for
status indicator

        }

      }

    });

  

    return NextResponse.json({ success: true, invoices }, { status: 200
});

  } catch (error: any) {

    console.error("\[FETCH INVOICES ERROR\]:", error.message);

    return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Failed to load
student ledger." }, { status: 500 });

  }

}

  

// POST: Generate a new tamper-proof invoice

export async function POST(req: Request) {

  try {

    const { studentId, category, session } = await req.json();

  

    if (!studentId \|\| !category \|\| !session) {

      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Student ID, Fee
Category, and Session are required." }, { status: 400 });

    }

  

    if (!(category in OFFICIAL_FEE_SCHEDULE)) {

      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Invalid
university fee category selected." }, { status: 400 });

    }

  

    const amount = OFFICIAL_FEE_SCHEDULE\[category as FeeCategory\];

  

    // Check if this fee has already been paid and cleared for the
selected session

    const existingPaid = await prisma.feeInvoice.findFirst({

      where: {

        studentId,

        category: category as FeeCategory,

        session,

        status: InvoiceStatus.PAID,

      },

    });

  

    if (existingPaid) {

      return NextResponse.json({

        success: false,

        error: "This fee category has already been paid and cleared for
the selected academic session.",

        isCleared: true,

      }, { status: 400 });

    }

  

    // Check if an unpaid invoice already exists for this exact fee and
session

    const existingPending = await prisma.feeInvoice.findFirst({

      where: {

        studentId,

        category: category as FeeCategory,

        session,

        status: InvoiceStatus.PENDING,

      },

    });

  

    if (existingPending) {

      return NextResponse.json({

        success: true,

        message: "Existing pending invoice retrieved.",

        invoice: existingPending,

        isExisting: true,

      }, { status: 200 });

    }

  

    // Create new invoice in SQLite ledger

    const newInvoice = await prisma.feeInvoice.create({

      data: {

        studentId,

        category: category as FeeCategory,

        amount,

        session,

        status: InvoiceStatus.PENDING,

      },

    });

  

    return NextResponse.json({

      success: true,

      message: "New invoice generated successfully.",

      invoice: newInvoice,

      isExisting: false,

    }, { status: 201 });

  } catch (error: any) {

    console.error("\[CREATE INVOICE ERROR\]:", error.message);

    return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Failed to
generate billing invoice." }, { status: 500 });

  }

}

You just exposed a classic edge-case vulnerability in financial
software: **Unchecked State Proliferation**.

This happened because of a loophole between our test script and your
invoice generation API:

1.  **The Script Injection:** When we ran `inject-fraud.ts`, it
    forcefully created a `BLOCKED` invoice for `ICT_INFRASTRUCTURE` in
    the database.

2.  **The API Loophole:** When you navigated to `/invoices` and clicked
    generate, your backend route (`/api/invoices/route.ts`) only checked
    if an invoice for that category was `PAID` or `PENDING`. **It did
    not check if an invoice was `BLOCKED`.** Because it didn't see a
    `PAID` or `PENDING` flag, it blindly generated a *second*
    `ICT_INFRASTRUCTURE` invoice!

In a real university portal, if a student gets blocked for fraud on a
fee, they shouldn't be able to just generate a fresh invoice for the
same fee to bypass the security freeze.

Here is how we permanently slam this loophole shut, followed by a quick
script to clean up your duplicate dashboard rows.

### Step 1: Patch the Invoice Generation Safeguard

We are upgrading your `POST` handler in `/api/invoices/route.ts` to
query for **ANY** existing invoice (`PAID`, `PENDING`, or `BLOCKED`). If
they try to generate an invoice for a category currently under a
`BLOCKED` security hold, the API rejects them immediately with a 403
Forbidden.

**WHERE:** `unizik-ml-fraud-frontend/src/app/api/invoices/route.ts`

**REPLACE:** Your entire `POST` function with this hardened version:

``` ng-tns-c3319599131-1854
// POST: Generate a new tamper-proof invoice with Zero-Trust state checking
export async function POST(req: Request) {
  try {
    const { studentId, category, session } = await req.json();

    if (!studentId || !category || !session) {
      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Student ID, Fee Category, and Session are required." }, { status: 400 });
    }

    if (!(category in OFFICIAL_FEE_SCHEDULE)) {
      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Invalid university fee category selected." }, { status: 400 });
    }

    const amount = OFFICIAL_FEE_SCHEDULE[category as FeeCategory];

    // CRITICAL FIX: Check if an invoice ALREADY exists in ANY state (PAID, PENDING, or BLOCKED)
    const existingInvoice = await prisma.feeInvoice.findFirst({
      where: {
        studentId,
        category: category as FeeCategory,
        session,
        status: {
          in: [InvoiceStatus.PAID, InvoiceStatus.PENDING, InvoiceStatus.BLOCKED]
        }
      },
    });

    if (existingInvoice) {
      // 1. If already PAID: Block new generation
      if (existingInvoice.status === InvoiceStatus.PAID) {
        return NextResponse.json({
          success: false,
          error: "This fee category has already been paid and cleared for the selected academic session.",
          isCleared: true,
        }, { status: 400 });
      }

      // 2. If under SECURITY HOLD (BLOCKED): Forbid generation! Force them to appeal!
      if (existingInvoice.status === InvoiceStatus.BLOCKED) {
        return NextResponse.json({
          success: false,
          error: "This fee obligation is currently suspended under a Bursary Security Hold. You must submit an administrative verification appeal before a new transaction can be initiated.",
          isBlocked: true,
        }, { status: 403 });
      }

      // 3. If PENDING: Return the existing pending invoice instead of creating a duplicate
      if (existingInvoice.status === InvoiceStatus.PENDING) {
        return NextResponse.json({
          success: true,
          message: "Existing pending invoice retrieved.",
          invoice: existingInvoice,
          isExisting: true,
        }, { status: 200 });
      }
    }

    // Create new invoice in SQLite ledger ONLY if no obligation exists for this session
    const newInvoice = await prisma.feeInvoice.create({
      data: {
        studentId,
        category: category as FeeCategory,
        amount,
        session,
        status: InvoiceStatus.PENDING,
      },
    });

    return NextResponse.json({
      success: true,
      message: "New invoice generated successfully.",
      invoice: newInvoice,
      isExisting: false,
    }, { status: 201 });
  } catch (error: any) {
    console.error("[CREATE INVOICE ERROR]:", error.message);
    return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Failed to generate billing invoice." }, { status: 500 });
  }
}
```

``` ng-tns-c3319599131-1855
// scripts/clean-duplicates.ts
import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client';
const prisma = new PrismaClient();

async function clean() {
  console.log('🧹 Scanning student ledger for duplicate or corrupted obligations...');

  // Find Sohail
  const student = await prisma.student.findFirst({ where: { matricNumber: '2022514009' } });
  if (!student) return;

  // Delete ANY invoice that is currently marked as BLOCKED or PENDING for ICT_INFRASTRUCTURE
  // This will leave ONLY his clean, paid invoices intact.
  const deleted = await prisma.feeInvoice.deleteMany({
    where: {
      studentId: student.id,
      category: 'ICT_INFRASTRUCTURE',
      status: {
        in: ['BLOCKED', 'PENDING']
      }
    }
  });

  console.log(`✨ Successfully purged ${deleted.count} duplicate/blocked invoice(s). Your ledger is now clean!`);
}

clean().finally(() => prisma.$disconnect());
```

You just hit the **1-to-1 Database Relational Constraint**. This is a
classic architectural safeguard working exactly as intended, but our API
route failed to handle the rejection gracefully.

### Why This Crashed

In your `schema.prisma`, look at how the `Appeal` table links to a
`Transaction`:

``` ng-tns-c3319599131-1857
transactionId  String  @unique @map("transaction_id")
```

Because of that `@unique` keyword, **a single transaction attempt can
only ever have ONE appeal record tied to it in the database.**

When you submitted the first time, it created the appeal successfully.
When you clicked submit a second time, your API blindly attempted
`prisma.appeal.create()` with the exact same `transactionId`. SQLite
immediately threw a fatal error to prevent duplicate records, and
because we didn't catch that specific collision, it bled raw database
code onto your UI.

### The Strategic Fix: Intelligent Upsert & Queue Checking

Instead of blindly creating a record, we must check if an appeal
*already exists* for this blocked transaction before writing to the
database:

1.  If an appeal already exists and is **`PENDING`**, we intercept them
    with a clean UI notice: *"An appeal is already queued for Chief
    Bursar review."*

2.  If an appeal was previously **`REJECTED`** by the Admin, we update
    the existing row with their new explanation and reset it to
    `PENDING` (allowing them to retry their appeal without violating the
    `@unique` constraint!).

### Code Fragment: Hardened Appeals POST Handler

**WHERE:** `unizik-ml-fraud-frontend/src/app/api/appeals/route.ts`

**REPLACE:** Your entire `POST` function with this self-defending
version:

``` ng-tns-c3319599131-1858
// POST: Student submits a dispute (Hardened against duplicate @unique collisions)
export async function POST(req: Request) {
  try {
    const { studentId, invoiceId, reason } = await req.json();

    if (!studentId || !invoiceId || !reason) {
      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Missing required dispute parameters." }, { status: 400 });
    }

    // 1. Find the latest blocked transaction associated with this invoice
    const tx = await prisma.transaction.findFirst({
      where: { invoiceId, studentId, status: 'BLOCKED' },
      orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' }
    });

    if (!tx) {
      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "No blocked transaction record found for this obligation." }, { status: 404 });
    }

    // 2. CRITICAL PRE-FLIGHT CHECK: Query if an appeal record already exists for this transaction
    const existingAppeal = await prisma.appeal.findUnique({
      where: { transactionId: tx.id }
    });

    if (existingAppeal) {
      // If it is already sitting in Dr. Ekeh's queue, forbid duplicate submissions
      if (existingAppeal.status === 'PENDING') {
        return NextResponse.json({ 
          success: false, 
          error: "A verification appeal has already been submitted for this security hold and is currently active in the Chief Bursar's review queue." 
        }, { status: 400 });
      }

      // If it was previously REJECTED, update the existing record with the new excuse instead of crashing!
      const resubmittedAppeal = await prisma.appeal.update({
        where: { transactionId: tx.id },
        data: {
          reason,
          status: 'PENDING',
          adminNotes: null // Clear out old admin rejection notes
        }
      });

      return NextResponse.json({ success: true, appeal: resubmittedAppeal, message: "Appeal resubmitted successfully." }, { status: 200 });
    }

    // 3. Create fresh appeal ONLY if no prior record exists for this transaction ID
    const appeal = await prisma.appeal.create({
      data: {
        transactionId: tx.id,
        studentId,
        reason,
        status: 'PENDING'
      }
    });

    return NextResponse.json({ success: true, appeal }, { status: 201 });
  } catch (error: any) {
    console.error("[APPEAL SUBMISSION ERROR]:", error.message);
    return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Failed to transmit appeal to administrative ledger." }, { status: 500 });
  }
}
```

</div>

</div>

### Why this solves it permanently:

1.  **Zero Raw Crashes:** The system will never throw a
    `Unique constraint failed` error again because we query `findUnique`
    before ever attempting a write.

2.  **Professional UX:** If you try to spam the submit button, the UI
    will cleanly display the red error banner: *"A verification appeal
    has already been submitted... currently active in the Chief Bursar's
    review queue."*

3.  **Resubmission Agency:** If Dr. Ekeh rejects a student's weak excuse
    (e.g., *"please unblock me"*), the student can come back to this
    page, write a better, detailed explanation, and submit it again. The
    API will cleanly update their old record back to `PENDING` without
    breaking the database relational map.

The **`Appeal`** is appended directly to the **`Transaction`** (via a
strict **one-to-one** `@unique` relational link), **not** the `Invoice`.

Here is the strategic, architectural breakdown of why this specific
relational mapping is mandatory for an enterprise-grade financial
security system—and exactly how you should defend it before your thesis
examiners.

## 1. Forensic Precision (The White-Box XAI Link)

An `Invoice` is strictly a **static financial obligation**—it only knows
*what* the student owes (e.g., ₦15,000 for ICT Infrastructure). It holds
zero environmental or behavioral data.

A `Transaction`, however, is a **dynamic security event**. It is the
exact cryptographic container that captured the failure. It holds:

- The user's browser fingerprint (`deviceId`)

- The routing origin (`ipAddress` and `asnNumber`)

- The behavioral velocity (`pageDwellTime`)

- The direct link to the **White-Box AI Audit Log** (`explanation`,
  `confidence`, and `verdict`)

When a student files an appeal, they are not disputing the *bill*—they
are disputing the **machine learning engine's security verdict on that
specific payment attempt**. By appending the `Appeal` directly to the
`Transaction`, you give the Chief Bursar (Dr. Ekeh) the ability to view
the student’s written excuse right next to the exact mathematical AI
telemetry that triggered the alarm.

## 2. Audit Trail Granularity (Handling Repeat Offenses)

Because an `Invoice` has a **one-to-many** relationship with
`Transactions`, a student might attempt to pay a single fee multiple
times over the course of a semester:

1.  **Monday at 10:00 AM:** Student attempts payment using a foreign
    VPN. The ML engine blocks it <span class="math-inline"
    math="\rightarrow"
    index-in-node="90"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml">$\rightarrow$</span><span class="katex-html"
    aria-hidden="true"><span class="katex-base"><span class="katex-strut"
    style="height: 0.3669em;"></span><span class="mrel">→</span></span></span></span></span>
    **`Transaction A (BLOCKED)`**.

2.  **Tuesday at 2:00 PM:** Student tries again using an automated
    script. The ML engine blocks it again <span class="math-inline"
    math="\rightarrow"
    index-in-node="97"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml">$\rightarrow$</span><span class="katex-html"
    aria-hidden="true"><span class="katex-base"><span class="katex-strut"
    style="height: 0.3669em;"></span><span class="mrel">→</span></span></span></span></span>
    **`Transaction B (BLOCKED)`**.

If your `Appeal` table were appended to the *Invoice*, the database
would suffer from **referential ambiguity**. When the admin opens the
dispute queue, they would have no way of knowing whether the student is
apologizing for Monday's VPN usage (`Transaction A`) or Tuesday's bot
script (`Transaction B`).

By enforcing a strict **one-to-one** link between `Appeal` and
`Transaction` (`transactionId String @unique`), every individual
security intercept gets its own isolated, tamper-proof dispute
container.

## 3. Separation of Concerns (Financial vs. Security Ledgers)

In software engineering and accounting governance, you must never mix
debt management with cyber-forensic exception handling:

- **The `FeeInvoice` Table** belongs exclusively to the **Financial
  Ledger** (managed by the Student Accounts Unit). Its only job is to
  track money owed versus money cleared.

- **The `Transaction`, `FraudAuditLog`, and `Appeal` Tables** belong
  exclusively to the **Security & Governance Ledger** (managed by the
  Revenue & Reconciliation Audit Engine).

Appending appeals to the invoice would pollute your clean financial
accounting tables with security dispute workflows, violating the
Object-Oriented Analysis and Design Methodology (OOADM) principles you
established in Section 3.1 of your project.

## The Upward Resolution Flow (How They Connect)

Even though the `Appeal` is attached to the bottom of the tree (the
`Transaction`), its approval flows upward to resolve the entire chain:

> rather than the Invoice table to preserve referential integrity and

> transaction represents a timestamped cryptographic event. Appending
> the dispute directly to the transaction ensures that administrative
> officers evaluate student remediation requests against the exact
> behavioral telemetry and explainable AI logs generated at the precise
> moment of interception."*

Here is the ruthless, simple explanation you can give to anyone—from a
non-technical professor to a software engineer—without getting tangled
in algorithmic jargon.

### Part 1: Why Must They Appeal Instead of Just Retrying? (Simple Words)

If an examiner asks: *"Why lock the student out? Why not just let them
try typing their card again?"*

Here is your exact, simple defense:

- **To Stop "Card Testing" by Cybercafe Scammers:** If we let people
  retry immediately after being blocked, a fraudulent cybercafe operator
  with a list of 50 stolen credit cards will simply sit on the portal,
  clicking "Pay Now" over and over until he finds a card that works. By
  freezing the invoice on the very first blocked attempt, we shut the
  door in the scammer's face. He cannot test another card.

- **A Block is an Alarm, Not a Typo:** If a student types the wrong
  password, that is a typo—let them retry. But our AI only blocks a
  payment if it detects **active deception** (like a bot moving at
  lightning speed, a foreign VPN, or a hardware mismatch). When an alarm
  goes off, you don't just reset it; you investigate who triggered it.

- **Real Students Can Explain; Scammers Cannot:** An innocent student
  whose laptop broke can easily send a quick message to the Bursary
  saying, *"I used the library desktop today."* The Bursar knows them
  and unlocks it. A cybercafe scammer using stolen cards cannot walk up
  to the Bursary to explain why he is paying from a suspicious network.
  The appeal process filters out the criminals.

### Part 2: What Actually Happens When Admin Clicks "Approved"? (What We Coded)

You are **100% correct** in your understanding. When Dr. Ekeh clicks
**"Approve Override & Unlock Invoice"**, we do **not** magically mark
the fee as paid, and we do **not** erase the blocked attempt.

Here is the exact, step-by-step breakdown of what our code executes
inside the database transaction block (`api/appeals/route.ts`):

#### 1. The Appeal Record <span class="math-inline" math="\rightarrow" index-in-node="21"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml">$\rightarrow$</span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="katex-base"><span class="katex-strut" style="height: 0.3669em;"></span><span class="mrel">→</span></span></span></span></span> Updated to `APPROVED`

The system updates the dispute ticket in the `Appeal` table from
`PENDING` to `APPROVED` and attaches a timestamped note: *"Manual
executive override executed by Chief Bursar."* This closes the ticket.

#### 2. The Transaction Record (The Attempt) <span class="math-inline" math="\rightarrow" index-in-node="40"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml">$\rightarrow$</span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="katex-base"><span class="katex-strut" style="height: 0.3669em;"></span><span class="mrel">→</span></span></span></span></span> REMAINS `BLOCKED` FOREVER

We **do not touch** the `Transaction` status. It stays as `BLOCKED` in
the database permanently.

- **Why?** Because that specific attempt at 3:14 PM *was* irregular. No
  money was taken during that attempt, and we must never rewrite
  history. It remains in the **White-Box Forensics Drawer** so the
  university auditors have permanent proof that the security perimeter
  did its job on that specific device and IP address.

#### 3. The Fee Invoice (The Bill) <span class="math-inline" math="\rightarrow" index-in-node="30"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml">$\rightarrow$</span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="katex-base"><span class="katex-strut" style="height: 0.3669em;"></span><span class="mrel">→</span></span></span></span></span> Changed from `BLOCKED` back to `PENDING`

This is the only thing the Admin override actually resets. Because the
parent `FeeInvoice` was frozen (`BLOCKED`), the student couldn't see the
checkout page. Our code runs this exact query:

Look closely at the second half of that OR condition:
`inv.transactions?.some(tx => tx.status === "BLOCKED")`.

Because we just agreed that **we never delete or alter historical
blocked transactions** (to preserve the white-box audit trail), that old
fraudulent attempt is still sitting inside `inv.transactions` with
`status: "BLOCKED"`.

Even though Dr. Ekeh approved the appeal and successfully changed the
parent `Invoice.status` back to `"PENDING"`, your frontend logic sees
that old transaction in the array, evaluates `isBlocked` as `true`, and
traps the student in an eternal UI loop!

### The Fix: Make `Invoice.status` the Single Source of Truth

Now that we are on **Path B**, the parent Invoice's status is the
supreme ruler of the security freeze. We must strip out the checks
against historical transactions so the UI obeys the Admin's override.

We need to patch **two files** right now:

loop.

  studentId: z.string().uuid(),

  invoiceId: z.string().uuid(),

  amount: z.number().positive(),

  reference: z.string().min(6),

  deviceId: z.string().min(8),

  pageDwellTime: z.number().positive(),

  hardwareMismatch: z.number().int().min(0).max(1),

});

  

/\*\*

 \* PRODUCTION NETWORK DETECTOR

 \* Detects if the user is on a Nigerian Telco (MTN, Glo, Airtel,
9Mobile).

 \* If not, flags as high risk (asnNumber = 1).

 \*/

async function getNetworkRiskScore(ip: string): Promise\<number\> {

  // 1. Localhost Handling

  if (ip === "127.0.0.1" \|\| ip === "::1" \|\|
ip.startsWith("192.168.")) return 0; // Safe in dev

  

  try {

    // Using free, no-key API: ip-api.com

    const response = await
fetch(\`http://ip-api.com/json/\${ip}?fields=status,isp,query\`);

    const data = await response.json();

  

    if (data.status !== "success") return 1; // Flag as risk if we can't
resolve IP

  

    const ispName = data.isp.toUpperCase();

    const telcos = \["MTN", "GLOBACOM", "AIRTEL", "9MOBILE",
"ETISALAT"\];

  

    // Check if the ISP string includes any of our whitelisted Nigerian
Telcos

    const isLocalTelco = telcos.some(telco =\> ispName.includes(telco));

  

    return isLocalTelco ? 0 : 1; // 0 = Safe (Local), 1 = Risky
(VPN/Foreign/Other)

  } catch (e) {

    console.error("\[NETWORK DETECTION ERROR\]", e);

    return 1; // Default to risky if detection fails

  }

}

  

export async function POST(req: Request) {

  try {

    const headersList = await headers();

    // Get real IP from headers

    const rawIp = headersList.get('x-forwarded-for') \|\| '127.0.0.1';

    const ipAddress = rawIp.split(',')\[0\]; // Handle proxy chains

  

    const body = await req.json();

    const validation = checkoutSchema.safeParse(body);

  

    if (!validation.success) {

      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Validation
Failed", details: validation.error }, { status: 400 });

    }

  

    // Server-side network risk assessment

    const asnNumber = await getNetworkRiskScore(ipAddress);

  

    // Merge client telemetry with server-derived network metadata

    const payload = {

      ...validation.data,

      ipAddress,

      asnNumber, // ENFORCED: Server overrides client's asnNumber

    };

  

    // 1. FINANCIAL INTEGRITY GUARDRAIL

    const invoice = await prisma.feeInvoice.findUnique({ where: { id:
payload.invoiceId } });

    if (!invoice \|\| invoice.studentId !== payload.studentId \|\|
invoice.amount !== payload.amount) {

      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Invalid or
Tampered Invoice" }, { status: 403 });

    }

    if (invoice.status === 'PAID') {

      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "This fee
invoice has already been cleared and marked as PAID in the university
records." }, { status: 400 });

    }

  

    // 2. DISPATCH TO ML ENGINE

    const engineResult = await evaluatePaymentTransaction(payload);

  

    // Use upsert to prevent "Unique constraint failed" on reference
collisions

    // and fix the status enum to match your schema ('CLEARED' vs
'SUCCESS')

    const tx = await prisma.transaction.upsert({

      where: { reference: payload.reference },

      update: {},

      create: {

        invoiceId: payload.invoiceId,

        studentId: payload.studentId,

        amount: payload.amount,

        reference: payload.reference,

        deviceId: payload.deviceId,

        ipAddress: payload.ipAddress,

        asnNumber: payload.asnNumber,

        pageDwellTime: payload.pageDwellTime,

        hardwareMismatch: payload.hardwareMismatch,

        status: engineResult.verdict === 'FRAUDULENT' ? 'BLOCKED' :
'CLEARED'

      }

    });

  

    if (engineResult.verdict === 'FRAUDULENT') {

      // CRITICAL PATH B ENFORCEMENT: Freeze the parent invoice
immediately

      await prisma.feeInvoice.update({

        where: { id: payload.invoiceId },

        data: { status: 'BLOCKED' as any }

      });

  

      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, message: "Blocked",
forensicReport: engineResult }, { status: 403 });

    }

  

    return NextResponse.json({ success: true, message: "Authorized",
data: { id: tx.id } }, { status: 200 });

  } catch (error: any) {

    console.error("\[CHECKOUT ROUTE ERROR\]:", error.message);

    return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Internal Error"
}, { status: 500 });

  }

}

### The Decision Tree Math (Gini Impurity in Action):

In Section 3.2 of your thesis, you defined the core environmental
threat: **Cybercafe Proxy Fraud**. What makes a cybercafe operator a
fraudster is that they act as a middleman, processing payments for
**multiple different students** from a single commercial computer using
stolen cards.

When your Python Decision Tree was trained, it used Gini Impurity to
find the most powerful feature to split legitimate students from
cybercafe criminals. That **Root Node (Primary Split)** is almost
certainly **`device_student_count_24h` (Velocity)**!

Here is how the algorithm evaluated your dummy attempt:

1.  **Root Question:** *Has this device attempted payments for

    different matriculation numbers in the last 24 hours?*

2.  **Your Data:** `device_student_count_24h == 1`

3.  **Internal Node:** *Are there multiple failed card attempts in the

4.  **Your Data:** `failed_attempts_1h == 1` <span class="math-inline"

5.  **Algorithmic Verdict:** Even though the user is on a VPN (`ASN: 1`)

### Why This is Pure Gold for Your Defense

If an examiner asks: *"Why use a complex Decision Tree instead of just
writing an `if/else` statement that blocks anyone on a VPN or typing too
fast?"*

You can present this exact terminal log as empirical evidence:

// unizik-ml-fraud-frontend/src/app/checkout/\[invoiceId\]/page.tsx

"use client";

  

import React, { useState, useEffect, useRef, use } from "react";

import { useRouter } from "next/navigation";

import { CreditCard, ArrowLeft, AlertCircle, RefreshCw, Lock, Building2,
AlertTriangle, CheckCircle2 } from "lucide-react";

import { generateDeviceFingerprint } from "@/lib/fingerprint";

import StudentHeader from "@/components/StudentHeader";

import BackButton from "@/components/BackButton";

  

export default function CheckoutPage({ params }: { params: Promise\<{
invoiceId: string }\> }) {

  const router = useRouter();

  const { invoiceId } = use(params);

  

  const \[user, setUser\] = useState\<any \| null\>(null);

  const \[invoice, setInvoice\] = useState\<any\>(null);

  const \[loading, setLoading\] = useState(true);

  const \[processing, setProcessing\] = useState(false);

  const \[deviceId, setDeviceId\] = useState("");

  const \[mismatch, setMismatch\] = useState(0);

  const \[paymentError, setPaymentError\] = useState\<string \|
null\>(null);

  

  // High-precision timer for behavioral dwell-time telemetry

  const startTime = useRef(performance.now());

  

  useEffect(() =\> {

    // 1. Retrieve authenticated student session

    const storedUser = localStorage.getItem("unizik_user");

    if (storedUser) {

      setUser(JSON.parse(storedUser));

    } else {

      router.push("/login");

      return;

    }

    fetch(\`/api/invoices?studentId=null&invoiceId=\${invoiceId}\`)

      .then((res) =\> res.json())

      .then((data) =\> {

        if (data.success) {

          setInvoice(data.invoice);

        } else {

          setPaymentError("Unable to load billing details for this
invoice.");

        }

      })

      .catch(() =\> setPaymentError("Network communication error with
the central ledger."));

  

    // 3. Initialize background telemetry

    const initTelemetry = async () =\> {

      const currentFP = await generateDeviceFingerprint();

      setDeviceId(currentFP);

      

      if (storedUser) {

        const parsedUser = JSON.parse(storedUser);

        if (parsedUser.loginDeviceId && parsedUser.loginDeviceId !==
currentFP) {

          setMismatch(1);

        }

      }

      setLoading(false);

    };

  

    initTelemetry();

  }, \[invoiceId, router\]);

  

  const handlePay = async () =\> {

    if (!user \|\| !invoice) return;

    

    setProcessing(true);

    setPaymentError(null);

  

    // Calculate real user dwell time in seconds

    const dwellTime = (performance.now() - startTime.current) / 1000;

    

    const payload = {

      studentId: user.id,

      invoiceId: invoiceId,

      amount: invoice.amount \|\| 0,

      reference: \`PAY\_\${Date.now().toString(36).toUpperCase()}
\_\${Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 7).toUpperCase()}\`,

      deviceId: deviceId,

      pageDwellTime: dwellTime,

      hardwareMismatch: mismatch,

    };

  

    try {

      const res = await fetch("/api/checkout", {

        method: "POST",

        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },

        body: JSON.stringify(payload)

      });

  

      const data = await res.json();

  

      if (res.ok && data.success) {

        const txId = data.data.id; 

        router.push(\`/receipt/\${txId}\`);

      } else {

        setPaymentError(data.error \|\| data.message \|\| "Transaction
declined by payment review. Please visit the Bursary desk.");

      }

    } catch (err) {

      setPaymentError("A network error occurred while processing your
transaction.");

    } finally {

      setProcessing(false);

    }

  };

  

  if (loading \|\| !invoice) {

    return (

      \<div className="min-h-screen bg-\[#F8FAFC\] flex flex-col
items-center justify-center text-slate-600 font-sans"\>

You are 100% right. Writing "Payment Routing Suspended due to irregular
session telemetry" on a student portal sounds like a bad sci-fi movie.
If a 100L student trying to pay an Acceptance fee sees that, they will
either panic or laugh. We need professional, human-centered
institutional wording—clear, firm, and easy to understand without
sacrificing the security narrative for your thesis.

Furthermore, your architectural insight on the state lockout is spot on.
By triggering `setInvoice((prev) => ({ ...prev, status: "BLOCKED" }))`
inside `handlePay`, React immediately re-renders the DOM, destroys the
payment form, and swaps in the lockout screen. Because the form and
button cease to exist, the student literally **cannot** spam the
database with multiple blocked requests. One strike and the door locks.

Here are the exact two fragments to apply to your checkout page.

### Fragment 1: The Instant State Lockout (Preventing DB Spam)

**WHERE:**
`unizik-ml-fraud-frontend/src/app/checkout/[invoiceId]/page.tsx`

**WHY:** When the API returns a fraud verdict, we instantly update the
local `invoice` state to `BLOCKED`. This forces React to unmount the
payment form immediately, preventing the user from clicking the button
again and flooding your ledger with duplicate blocked attempts.

Replace the `if (res.ok && data.success)` check inside your `handlePay`
function with this exact logic:

This is a critical edge case. In a thesis defense, the professors will
look for the "failure states." If you only show how the system works
when it works, you haven't built a robust system.

Here is the simple, professional way to handle a rejection, both in your
**thesis defense speech** and in your **actual code**.

### 1. The Thesis Defense Answer (Keep it Simple)

When they ask, *"How does a student know if their appeal is rejected?"*,
do not say "we send an email" (that's scope creep).

**Say this:**

> "The system is built on **Passive Transparency**. We do not rely on
> external notifications like email, which can be missed or spoofed.
> Instead, the student portal acts as the 'Single Source of Truth.' When
> a student logs into their dashboard, they see the real-time status of
> their dispute request. If an appeal is rejected, the status updates to
> 'Review Concluded: Not Approved,' and the system guides them to the
> next administrative step, such as visiting the Bursary office for a
> manual audit."

### 2. The UX Strategy: How they see it

We will update your **Student Dashboard** to show the Appeal Status once
it is reviewed. This turns your "Appeal" button into an "Appeal Status"
badge.

**Where to update:** `src/app/dashboard/page.tsx`

Replace your existing logic in the table where you display actions. We
will add a check: if an appeal exists for that invoice and it was
rejected, show the rejection status.

### 3. Summary of the Workflow (The "Simple" version)

If they ask, here is the clear path for the student:

1.  **Submission:** Student submits an appeal because the system blocked
    them.

2.  **Dashboard:** The button changes from "Request Review" to "Appeal
    Pending." (This lets the student know the Bursar is reading it).

3.  **Outcome:**

    - **Approved:** The dashboard updates, the badge disappears, and
      "Pay Now" returns.

    - **Rejected:** The badge updates to "Review Concluded: Not
      Approved."

4.  **Finality:** At this stage, the student is prompted to "Resubmit
    Appeal" (if they have new evidence) or they are directed to the
    Bursary office.

**This shows the professors that your system doesn't just block
people—it manages the entire relationship between the University and the
Student.**

Does this status flow make sense for your thesis, or do you want to add
a specific "Rejection Reason" field where the admin can type why they
said no?

ShieldCheck, AlertCircle, Shield, Cpu } from "lucide-react";

  interface Invoice {

    id: string;

    category: string;

    amount: number;

    session: string;

    status: "PENDING" \| "PAID" \| "CANCELLED" \| "BLOCKED";

    createdAt: string;

    transactions: Array\<{ id: string; status: string; reference?:
string }\>;

  }

  

  export default function StudentDashboard() {

    const router = useRouter();

    const \[user, setUser\] = useState\<any \| null\>(null);

    const \[invoices, setInvoices\] = useState\<Invoice\[\]\>(\[\]);

    const \[loading, setLoading\] = useState(true);

    const \[error, setError\] = useState\<string \| null\>(null);

  

    useEffect(() =\> {

      // Retrieve authenticated session

      const storedUser = localStorage.getItem("unizik_user");

      if (!storedUser) {

        router.push("/login");

        return;

      }

  

      const parsedUser = JSON.parse(storedUser);

      setUser(parsedUser);

  

      // Fetch student ledger

      fetch(\`/api/invoices?studentId=\${parsedUser.id}\`)

        .then((res) =\> res.json())

        .then((data) =\> {

          if (data.success) {

            setInvoices(data.invoices);

          } else {

            setError(data.error);

          }

        })

        .catch(() =\> setError("Failed to synchronize with university
ledger."))

        .finally(() =\> setLoading(false));

    }, \[router\]);

  

    if (loading \|\| !user) {

      return (

        \<div className="min-h-screen bg-\[#F8FAFC\] flex flex-col
items-center justify-center text-slate-600 font-sans"\>

          \<div className="w-8 h-8 border-3 border-\[#001C3D\]/20
border-t-\[#001C3D\] rounded-full animate-spin mb-3" /\>

text-\[#001C3D\]"\>

          \</span\>

        \</div\>

      );

    }

  

    const totalPaid = invoices

      .filter((inv) =\> inv.status === "PAID")

      .reduce((sum, inv) =\> sum + inv.amount, 0);

  

    const pendingCount = invoices.filter((inv) =\> inv.status ===
"PENDING").length;

  

    return (

font-sans pb-16 selection:bg-\[#001C3D\] selection:text-white"\>

``` ng-tns-c3319599131-1871
                              <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 bg-emerald-50 text-emerald-700 border border-emerald-200 px-3 py-1 rounded-full font-sans text-[11px] font-bold shadow-2xs">
                                <CheckCircle className="w-3.5 h-3.5 text-emerald-600" />
                                <span>PAID &amp; CLEARED</span>
                              </span>
                            ) : isBlocked ? (
                              hasPendingAppeal ? (
                                /* STATE 1: APPEAL PENDING IN BURSAR'S QUEUE */
                                <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 bg-blue-50 text-blue-800 border border-blue-200 px-3 py-1 rounded-full font-sans text-[11px] font-bold shadow-2xs">
                                  <Clock className="w-3.5 h-3.5 text-blue-600 animate-pulse" />
                                  <span>REVIEW PENDING</span>
                                </span>
                              ) : hasRejectedAppeal ? (
                                /* STATE 2: APPEAL REJECTED BY BURSAR */
                                <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 bg-rose-50 text-rose-900 border border-rose-300 px-3 py-1 rounded-full font-sans text-[11px] font-bold shadow-2xs">
                                  <Shield className="w-3.5 h-3.5 text-rose-700" />
                                  <span>REVIEW CONCLUDED: NOT APPROVED</span>
                                </span>
                              ) : (
                                /* STATE 3: BLOCKED WITH NO APPEAL SUBMITTED YET */
                                <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 bg-rose-50 text-rose-800 border border-rose-200 px-3 py-1 rounded-full font-sans text-[11px] font-bold shadow-2xs">
                                  <Shield className="w-3.5 h-3.5 text-rose-600" />
                                  <span>SECURITY HOLD</span>
                                </span>
                              )
                            ) : (
                              /* STATE 4: NORMAL PENDING CLEARANCE (OR APPROVED OVERRIDE BACK TO PENDING) */
                              <span className="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 bg-amber-50 text-amber-800 border border-amber-200/80 px-3 py-1 rounded-full font-sans text-[11px] font-bold shadow-2xs">
                                <Clock className="w-3.5 h-3.5 text-amber-600" />
                                <span>PENDING CLEARANCE</span>
                              </span>
                            )}
                          </td>
                          <td className="py-4 px-6 text-right font-sans">
                            {isPaid ? (
                              <button
                                onClick={() => {
                                  const clearedTx = inv.transactions?.find(tx => tx.status === "CLEARED" || tx.status === "SUCCESS");
                                  const txId = clearedTx?.id || (inv as any).reference || inv.id;
                                  router.push(`/receipt/${txId}`);
                                }}
                                className="px-3.5 py-1.5 bg-emerald-600 hover:bg-emerald-500 active:scale-[0.98] text-white rounded-xl font-bold text-xs transition-all duration-200 shadow-2xs flex items-center gap-1.5 ml-auto cursor-pointer"
                              >
                                <FileText className="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
                                <span>View Receipt</span>
                              </button>
                            ) : isBlocked ? (
                              hasPendingAppeal ? (
                                /* Disabled state while waiting for Admin to review */
                                <button
                                  disabled
                                  className="px-4 py-2 bg-slate-100 text-slate-400 border border-slate-200 rounded-xl font-bold text-xs flex items-center gap-1.5 ml-auto cursor-not-allowed"
                                >
                                  <Clock className="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
                                  <span>Under Review</span>
                                </button>
                              ) : hasRejectedAppeal ? (
                                /* Lets student try submitting a better explanation if rejected */
                                <button
                                  onClick={() => router.push(`/support/appeal?invoiceId=${inv.id}`)}
                                  className="px-4 py-2 bg-slate-800 hover:bg-slate-900 active:scale-[0.98] text-white rounded-xl font-bold text-xs transition-all duration-200 shadow-sm flex items-center gap-1.5 ml-auto cursor-pointer"
                                >
                                  <AlertCircle className="w-3.5 h-3.5 text-rose-400" />
                                  <span>Resubmit Appeal</span>
                                </button>
                              ) : (
                                /* Initial button to submit an appeal */
                                <button
                                  onClick={() => router.push(`/support/appeal?invoiceId=${inv.id}`)}
                                  className="px-4 py-2 bg-rose-600 hover:bg-rose-700 active:scale-[0.98] text-white rounded-xl font-bold text-xs transition-all duration-200 shadow-sm shadow-rose-500/20 flex items-center gap-1.5 ml-auto cursor-pointer"
                                >
                                  <AlertCircle className="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
                                  <span>Request Review</span>
                                </button>
                              )
                            ) : (
                              /* Standard Pay Now button (shows up initially or after an Admin APPROVES an appeal) */
                              <button
                                onClick={() => router.push(`/checkout/${inv.id}`)}
                                className="px-4 py-2 bg-[#F58220] hover:bg-[#d97016] active:scale-[0.98] text-white rounded-xl font-bold text-xs transition-all duration-200 shadow-sm shadow-orange-500/20 flex items-center gap-1.5 ml-auto cursor-pointer"
                              >
                                <CreditCard className="w-3.5 h-3.5" />
                                <span>Pay Now</span>
                              </button>
                            )}
                          </td>
                        </tr>
                      );
                    })}
```

### What Noticeably Changes for the Student:

1.  **When they submit an appeal:** The red badge turns into a calm blue
    **REVIEW PENDING** badge with a pulsing clock, and the button
    changes to a disabled **Under Review** state so they know Dr. Ekeh
    is reading it.

2.  **If Dr. Ekeh clicks Reject:** The badge turns into a firm **REVIEW
    CONCLUDED: NOT APPROVED**, and the button updates to a dark
    **Resubmit Appeal** button so they can try explaining again.

3.  **If Dr. Ekeh clicks Approve:** The invoice reverts cleanly back to
    your original amber **PENDING CLEARANCE**, and the orange **Pay
    Now** button returns exactly as coded!

}\>;

}

// unizik-ml-fraud-frontend/prisma/schema.prisma

  

generator client {

  provider = "prisma-client-js"

}

  

datasource db {

  provider = "sqlite"

  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")

}

  

enum InvoiceStatus {

  PENDING

  PAID

  CANCELLED

  BLOCKED

}

  

enum TransactionStatus {

  PENDING

  CLEARED

  BLOCKED

  FAILED

}

  

enum FeeCategory {

  TUITION

  ACCEPTANCE

  ICT_INFRASTRUCTURE

  LIBRARY

  EXAM_CLEARANCE

}

  

enum AppealStatus {

  PENDING

  APPROVED

  REJECTED

}

  

model Student {

  id             String          @id @default(uuid())

  matricNumber   String          @unique @map("matric_number")

  email          String          @unique

  password       String          // Hashed bcrypt password

  firstName      String          @map("first_name")

  lastName       String          @map("last_name")

  department     String

  level          Int             // e.g., 100, 200, 300, 400, 500

  loginDeviceId  String?         @map("login_device_id") // Baseline
hardware hash captured at login

  createdAt      DateTime        @default(now()) @map("created_at")

  updatedAt      DateTime        @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  

  // Relational links

  invoices       FeeInvoice\[\]

  transactions   Transaction\[\]

  auditLogs      FraudAuditLog\[\]

  appeals        Appeal\[\]

  

  @@map("students")

}

  

model Admin {

  id             String          @id @default(uuid())

  username       String          @unique

  password       String          // Hashed bcrypt password

  fullName       String          @map("full_name")

  role           String          @default("BURSARY_OFFICER") // e.g.,
BURSARY_OFFICER, ICT_DIRECTOR

  createdAt      DateTime        @default(now()) @map("created_at")

  

  @@map("admins")

}

  

model FeeInvoice {

  id             String          @id @default(uuid())

  studentId      String          @map("student_id")

  category       FeeCategory

  amount         Float           // Float used for SQLite compatibility

  session        String          // e.g., "2025/2026"

  status         InvoiceStatus   @default(PENDING)

  createdAt      DateTime        @default(now()) @map("created_at")

  updatedAt      DateTime        @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  

  // Relational links

  student        Student         @relation(fields: \[studentId\],
references: \[id\], onDelete: Restrict)

  transactions   Transaction\[\]

  

  @@index(\[studentId, status\])

  @@map("fee_invoices")

}

  

model Transaction {

  id               String            @id @default(uuid())

  reference        String            @unique

  invoiceId        String            @map("invoice_id")

  studentId        String            @map("student_id")

  amount           Float

  status           TransactionStatus @default(PENDING)

  

  // Security & ML Extraction Fields (The Data Feed for Python)

  deviceId         String            @map("device_id") // Current
browser fingerprint hash

  ipAddress        String            @map("ip_address")

  asnNumber        Int               @default(0) @map("asn_number")

  pageDwellTime    Float             @map("page_dwell_time")

  isOffPeak        Int               @default(0) @map("is_off_peak")

  hardwareMismatch Int               @default(0)
@map("hardware_mismatch")

  

  createdAt        DateTime          @default(now()) @map("created_at")

  updatedAt        DateTime          @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  

  // Relational links

  invoice          FeeInvoice        @relation(fields: \[invoiceId\],
references: \[id\], onDelete: Restrict)

  student          Student           @relation(fields: \[studentId\],
references: \[id\], onDelete: Restrict)

  auditLog         FraudAuditLog?

  appeal           Appeal?

  

  @@index(\[deviceId, createdAt\])

  @@index(\[studentId, status, createdAt\])

  @@index(\[deviceId, studentId, createdAt\])

  @@map("transactions")

}

  

model FraudAuditLog {

  id             String      @id @default(uuid())

  transactionId  String      @unique @map("transaction_id")

  studentId      String      @map("student_id")

  prediction     Int         // 0 = Legitimate, 1 = Fraudulent

  confidence     Float       // AI Probability score

  verdict        String      // "LEGITIMATE" or "FRAUDULENT"

  explanation    String      // Complete white-box justification string

  createdAt      DateTime    @default(now()) @map("created_at")

  

  // Relational links

  transaction    Transaction @relation(fields: \[transactionId\],
references: \[id\], onDelete: Cascade)

  student        Student     @relation(fields: \[studentId\],
references: \[id\], onDelete: Cascade)

  

  @@index(\[verdict, createdAt\])

  @@map("fraud_audit_logs")

}

  

model Appeal {

  id             String       @id @default(uuid())

  transactionId  String       @unique @map("transaction_id")

  studentId      String       @map("student_id")

  reason         String       // Student's explanation for
false-positive anomaly

  status         AppealStatus @default(PENDING)

  adminNotes     String?      @map("admin_notes")

  createdAt      DateTime     @default(now()) @map("created_at")

  updatedAt      DateTime     @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  

  // Relational links

  transaction    Transaction  @relation(fields: \[transactionId\],
references: \[id\], onDelete: Cascade)

  student        Student      @relation(fields: \[studentId\],
references: \[id\], onDelete: Cascade)

  

  @@index(\[status, createdAt\])

  @@map("appeals")

}

Here is the ruthless, unbiased diagnosis of why your UI broke and showed
"Pay Now" on a rejected appeal—and why your proposed 3-step state logic
is the exact architectural upgrade needed.

As requested: **No code yet. Diagnosis only.**

### 1. The Diagnosis: Why Did It Show "Pay Now" After Rejection?

There are two distinct flaws currently fighting each other inside your
dashboard state machine:

#### Flaw A: The Historical Array Trap (`.some()`)

In our previous patch, we used `.some()` to check appeal statuses:

``` ng-tns-c3319599131-1872
const hasRejectedAppeal = inv.transactions?.some(tx => tx.appeal?.status === "REJECTED");
```

In software architecture, using `.some()` on a historical transaction
ledger is a fatal flaw. Why? Because `.some()` scans the **entire
history from the beginning of time**. If Sohail had a payment attempt
blocked on Monday that was *rejected*, but on Tuesday he submitted a new
attempt or a new appeal, `.some()` will still see Monday's rejection and
mix up the UI state.

#### Flaw B: Desynchronized Ledger States

Why did you see "Pay Now"? Because when Dr. Ekeh clicked **REJECT** on
the admin dashboard, our backend updated `appeal.status = 'REJECTED'`,
but if that specific invoice was generated before our recent database
patch (or if `inv.status` was somehow still sitting at `"PENDING"`), the
frontend looked at it and said: *"Well, `isBlocked` evaluates to false,
so let me fall back to the default: PENDING CLEARANCE and Pay Now!"*

### 2. The Solution: The "Latest Attempt" Rule (`latestTx`)

Your instinct is 100% correct. To make this system fail-secure, we must
stop scanning the whole transaction array with `.some()` and stop
relying on just `inv.status`.

Instead, because your backend already sorts transactions by newest first
(`orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' }`), **the single source of truth for
your UI must always be the Most Recent Transaction Attempt
(`latestTx = inv.transactions?.[0]`)**.

Here is the exact, bulletproof 4-State Matrix we should implement:

### The 4-State Matrix (How it will evaluate)

When the dashboard loads an invoice that is NOT paid
(`status !== "PAID"`), it looks directly at the newest transaction
attempt (`latestTx`) and evaluates this exact sequence:

- **State 1: The Fresh Block (No Appeal Yet)**

  - **Condition:** `latestTx.status === "BLOCKED"` AND `latestTx.appeal`
    does not exist.

  - **UI Badge:** Red **SECURITY HOLD**

  - **Action Button:** Red **Request Review** (Routes to
    `/support/appeal`)

- **State 2: The Active Review (Appeal Pending)**

  - **Condition:** `latestTx.status === "BLOCKED"` AND
    `latestTx.appeal.status === "PENDING"`.

  - **UI Badge:** Blue **REVIEW PENDING** (Pulsing icon)

  - **Action Button:** Grey **Under Review** (Disabled—cannot be clicked
    so they don't spam Dr. Ekeh).

- **State 3: The Bursar Rejection (Appeal Rejected)**

  - **Condition:** `latestTx.status === "BLOCKED"` AND
    `latestTx.appeal.status === "REJECTED"`.

  - **UI Badge:** Dark Red **REVIEW CONCLUDED: NOT APPROVED**

  - **Action Button:** Dark Slate **Resubmit Appeal** (Allows them to
    submit a better explanation to try again). *This is where your
    system previously failed and showed "Pay Now"!*

- **State 4: The Approved Override (Gateway Restored)**

  - **Condition:** `latestTx.status === "BLOCKED"` AND
    `latestTx.appeal.status === "APPROVED"` (OR no blocked transaction
    exists at all).

  - **UI Badge:** Amber **PENDING CLEARANCE**

  - **Action Button:** Orange **Pay Now** (Unlocks gateway access so
    they can finally pay!).

### Why This Design is Thesis-Ready

If a defense panel professor asks: *"What happens if an admin rejects an
appeal, but the student tries to bypass the rejection by clicking pay
again?"*

With this diagnosis applied, your answer is airtight:

> *"Our frontend state machine evaluates the cryptographic head of the
> transaction ledger—the most recent transaction attempt. If the latest
> attempt holds an appeal record with a REJECTED syntax from the Chief
> Bursar, the gateway routing button ('Pay Now') remains strictly
> unrendered from the DOM. The student is restricted entirely to the
> remediation loop ('Resubmit Appeal') until an administrative officer
> explicitly grants an APPROVED override."*

### Ready for the Code?

This matrix eliminates the bug you just witnessed and ensures a rejected
appeal **never** shows "Pay Now" again.

If this 4-State Matrix matches your strategic vision, give me the
command and I will give you the clean, surgical snippet for
`dashboard/page.tsx`.

### The Diagnosis: Why Your Dashboard is Blind

This is a classic data serialization failure. Your frontend logic is not
broken—**your backend query is starving the frontend of data.**

Here is what is happening: When the Student Dashboard loads, it calls
`/api/invoices?studentId=...`. In your backend route
(`/api/invoices/route.ts`), look at how Prisma is querying the database:

Because Prisma excludes nested relational tables by default unless
explicitly instructed via `include`, your `/api/invoices` API is sending
`transactions` to the frontend **without their attached `appeal` data**.

When your dashboard code runs
`const appealStatus = latestTx?.appeal?.status;`, it evaluates to
`undefined` for every single row. When `appealStatus` is `undefined`:

1.  It is not `"PENDING"`, so it skips the blue badge.

2.  It is not `"REJECTED"`, so it skips the dark red badge.

3.  It is not `"APPROVED"`, so `appealStatus !== "APPROVED"` evaluates
    to `true`, trapping even your approved ACCEPTANCE fee in the
    fallback red **SECURITY HOLD** state!

`return`:

### Step 2: The Surgical Backend Fix

Once you confirm via the logs that the API is dropping the appeal data,
the fix is a single 1-line query update in your backend invoice handler.

We need to tell Prisma to explicitly join and serialize the `appeal`
table when it pulls the `transactions` array in
`/api/invoices/route.ts`.

// unizik-ml-fraud-frontend/src/app/api/invoices/route.ts

  

import { NextResponse } from 'next/server';

import { prisma } from '@/lib/prisma';

import { FeeCategory, InvoiceStatus } from '@prisma/client';

  

// Official UNIZIK Fee Schedule (Server-Enforced to prevent client-side
price tampering)

const OFFICIAL_FEE_SCHEDULE: Record\<FeeCategory, number\> = {

  TUITION: 85500.00,

  ACCEPTANCE: 45000.00,

  ICT_INFRASTRUCTURE: 15000.00,

  LIBRARY: 5000.00,

  EXAM_CLEARANCE: 10000.00,

};

  

// GET: Fetch all invoices for a specific student UUID

export async function GET(req: Request) {

  try {

    const { searchParams } = new URL(req.url);

    const studentId = searchParams.get('studentId');

    const invoiceId = searchParams.get('invoiceId');

   

    if (invoiceId) {

        const invoice = await prisma.feeInvoice.findUnique({ where: {
id: invoiceId } });

        return NextResponse.json({ success: true, invoice });

    }

    if (!studentId) {

      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Student UUID is
required." }, { status: 400 });

    }

  

    const invoices = await prisma.feeInvoice.findMany({

      where: { studentId },

      orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' },

      include: {

        transactions: {

          orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' },

          take: 1, // Include the most recent transaction attempt for
status indicator

        }

      }

    });

  

    return NextResponse.json({ success: true, invoices }, { status: 200
});

  } catch (error: any) {

    console.error("\[FETCH INVOICES ERROR\]:", error.message);

    return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Failed to load
student ledger." }, { status: 500 });

  }

}

  

// POST: Generate a new tamper-proof invoice with Zero-Trust state
checking

export async function POST(req: Request) {

  try {

    const { studentId, category, session } = await req.json();

  

    if (!studentId \|\| !category \|\| !session) {

      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Student ID, Fee
Category, and Session are required." }, { status: 400 });

    }

  

    if (!(category in OFFICIAL_FEE_SCHEDULE)) {

      return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Invalid
university fee category selected." }, { status: 400 });

    }

  

    const amount = OFFICIAL_FEE_SCHEDULE\[category as FeeCategory\];

  

    // CRITICAL FIX: Check if an invoice ALREADY exists in ANY state
(PAID, PENDING, or BLOCKED)

    const existingInvoice = await prisma.feeInvoice.findFirst({

      where: {

        studentId,

        category: category as FeeCategory,

        session,

        status: {

          in: \[InvoiceStatus.PAID, InvoiceStatus.PENDING,
InvoiceStatus.BLOCKED\]

        }

      },

    });

  

    if (existingInvoice) {

      // 1. If already PAID: Block new generation

      if (existingInvoice.status === InvoiceStatus.PAID) {

        return NextResponse.json({

          success: false,

          error: "This fee category has already been paid and cleared
for the selected academic session.",

          isCleared: true,

        }, { status: 400 });

      }

  

      // 2. If under SECURITY HOLD (BLOCKED): Forbid generation! Force
them to appeal!

      if (existingInvoice.status === InvoiceStatus.BLOCKED) {

        return NextResponse.json({

          success: false,

          error: "This fee obligation is currently suspended under a
Bursary Security Hold. You must submit an administrative verification
appeal before a new transaction can be initiated.",

          isBlocked: true,

        }, { status: 403 });

      }

  

      // 3. If PENDING: Return the existing pending invoice instead of
creating a duplicate

      if (existingInvoice.status === InvoiceStatus.PENDING) {

        return NextResponse.json({

          success: true,

          message: "Existing pending invoice retrieved.",

          invoice: existingInvoice,

          isExisting: true,

        }, { status: 200 });

      }

    }

  

    // Create new invoice in SQLite ledger ONLY if no obligation exists
for this session

    const newInvoice = await prisma.feeInvoice.create({

      data: {

        studentId,

        category: category as FeeCategory,

        amount,

        session,

        status: InvoiceStatus.PENDING,

      },

    });

  

    return NextResponse.json({

      success: true,

      message: "New invoice generated successfully.",

      invoice: newInvoice,

      isExisting: false,

    }, { status: 201 });

  } catch (error: any) {

    console.error("\[CREATE INVOICE ERROR\]:", error.message);

    return NextResponse.json({ success: false, error: "Failed to
generate billing invoice." }, { status: 500 });

  }

}

render the blue **REVIEW PENDING** and dark red **REVIEW CONCLUDED: NOT
APPROVED** badges.

``` ng-tns-c3319599131-1878
const isActivelyBlocked = (inv.status === "BLOCKED" || latestTx?.status === "BLOCKED") && appealStatus !== "APPROVED";
```

This line is the absolute master key to the system. When the Admin
clicks **APPROVED**:

1.  The backend changes the invoice status from `"BLOCKED"` back to
    `"PENDING"`.

2.  The backend changes the appeal status to `"APPROVED"`.

When the student's dashboard refreshes, it evaluates that line:

- `inv.status` is no longer `"BLOCKED"`.

- Even though `latestTx.status` is still `"BLOCKED"` (because we keep
  the historical record), the second half of the statement kicks in.

- `appealStatus !== "APPROVED"` evaluates to **FALSE**.

Because of that `FALSE`, the variable `isActivelyBlocked` instantly
collapses to `false`.

### The UI Fallback (State 4)

Because `isPaid` is false and `isActivelyBlocked` is false, your UI
automatically skips all the red and blue blocked states and falls
straight down to the final `else` block (Lines 226 and 264):

// unizik-ml-fraud-frontend/src/app/admin/appeals/page.tsx

"use client";

  

import React, { useState, useEffect } from "react";

import { useRouter } from "next/navigation";

import { ShieldCheck, XCircle, CheckCircle2, AlertTriangle, RefreshCw,
Cpu, FileText } from "lucide-react";

import AdminHeader from "@/components/AdminHeader";

import BackButton from "@/components/BackButton";

  

export default function AdminAppealsPage() {

  const router = useRouter();

  const \[appeals, setAppeals\] = useState\<any\[\]\>(\[\]);

  const \[loading, setLoading\] = useState(true);

  const \[actionLoading, setActionLoading\] = useState\<string \|
null\>(null);

  

  const fetchAppeals = () =\> {

    setLoading(true);

    fetch("/api/appeals")

      .then((res) =\> res.json())

      .then((data) =\> {

        if (data.success) setAppeals(data.appeals);

      })

      .finally(() =\> setLoading(false));

  };

  

  useEffect(() =\> {

    const storedUser = localStorage.getItem("unizik_user");

    if (!storedUser) {

      router.push("/login");

      return;

    }

    const parsedUser = JSON.parse(storedUser);

    if (parsedUser.role !== "ADMIN" && parsedUser.role !==
"BURSARY_DIRECTOR") {

      router.push("/dashboard");

      return;

    }

    fetchAppeals();

  }, \[router\]);

  

  const handleAction = async (appealId: string, status: "APPROVED" \|
"REJECTED") =\> {

    setActionLoading(appealId);

    try {

      const res = await fetch("/api/appeals", {

        method: "PATCH",

        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },

        body: JSON.stringify({ appealId, status, adminNotes: \`Manual
executive override executed by Chief Bursar on \${new
Date().toLocaleDateString()}\` })

      });

      if (res.ok) fetchAppeals();

    } finally {

                      \<p className="text-rose-950 font-semibold
text-\[11px\]"\>{auditLog?.explanation \|\| "Anomalous hardware

                  {/\* Administrative Action Bar \*/}

                  {isPending && (

pt-2 border-t border-slate-100"\>

                      \<button

                        disabled={actionLoading === item.id}

                        onClick={() =\> handleAction(item.id,
"REJECTED")}

                        className="px-4 py-2 bg-slate-100
hover:bg-slate-200 text-slate-700 rounded-xl text-xs font-bold
transition-all cursor-pointer disabled:opacity-50"

                      \>

                        Reject Dispute

                      \</button\>

                      \<button

                        disabled={actionLoading === item.id}

                        onClick={() =\> handleAction(item.id,
"APPROVED")}

                        className="px-5 py-2 bg-emerald-600
hover:bg-emerald-500 text-white rounded-xl text-xs font-bold
transition-all shadow-sm shadow-emerald-600/20 cursor-pointer flex
items-center gap-1.5 disabled:opacity-50"

                      \>

                        \<ShieldCheck className="w-4 h-4" /\>

                        \<span\>Approve Override &amp; Unblock
Invoice\</span\>

                      \</button\>

                    \</div\>

                  )}

                \</div\>

              );

            })

          )}

        \</div\>

      \</main\>

    \</div\>

  );

}

You are 100% right. Stacking massive, multi-line cards vertically
without a search bar or filter tabs is amateurish. In a real
institutional deployment with hundreds of students, that layout would
become an unusable scrolling nightmare within 48 hours.

An enterprise-grade fraud control center (like Stripe Radar or Sift
Science) uses a **High-Density Data Grid with Filter Tabs, Live Search,
and Expandable Forensic Drawers**.

Here is the complete structural overhaul of your Admin Appeals screen.

### Why This Redesign is Industry-Standard & Thesis-Ready:

1.  **Instant Filtering Tabs:** Live counters for `All`,
    `Pending Review` (defaulting here so Dr. Ekeh sees work first),
    `Approved Overrides`, and `Rejected Disputes`.

2.  **Real-Time Search Engine:** Search instantly by Matriculation
    Number, Student Name, or Fee Category.

3.  **High-Density Compact Table:** Fits 15+ appeals on a single screen
    instead of 3.

4.  **Expandable White-Box Forensics:** Instead of cramming text on the
    main screen, the admin clicks **"View Forensics & Reason"** to
    smoothly slide open a dedicated XAI telemetry drawer right beneath
    the row.

5.  **1-Click Executive Action:** Approve or Reject buttons sit right in
    the grid row with spinning loading states.

### Complete Production File: `src/app/admin/appeals/page.tsx`

Replace your entire file with this self-contained, enterprise-grade
version:
